subject: [RFC PATCH v3 3/8] mm/gup: split follow_page_pte_commit() out of follow_page_pte()

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David (Arm) suggested that the function name and abstraction of follow_page_pte_commit() are not ideal, as it requires internal documentation to understand its purpose. He also proposed removing the pte parameter and instead passing in the result of pte_dirty(), and further suggested making the function capable of handling PMD/PUDs in addition to PTEs.
reviews.raw_body:
If a function needs 4 lines of internal doc to understand what it does, then
maybe it's not the right function name or abstraction. :)

I don't particularly enjoy the "commit" terminology, it looses the detail of the
most important thing this function is supposed to to: grab a folio reference.

We're passing in the pte only to do a single pte_dirty(). If the helper is
actually what we want, likely we just just pass in the pte_dirty() directly and
remove all pte leftovers from the helper.

I'd assume that we'd want a function where we can similarly punch in a PMD/PUD
and have it do the same thing as well, instead of special-casing ptes.

Let me think about this some more, I might have to play with the code myself to
understand how this should all be cleaned up.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author noticed that the pmd and pud code does not call mark_folio_dirty() when needed, which could be a problem for huge folios coming from a filesystem; author is willing to do necessary cleanups.
reviews.raw_body:
Looking at the differences between the pte and pmd
code, there is another big thing that stands out.

The pte code will call mark_folio_dirty() when
needed, but the pmd and pud code do not.

For hugetlbfs we can get away with that, but for
huge folios coming from a filesystem, don't we
want to call mark_folio_dirty() somewhere?

I'm happy to do whatever cleanups we can do to
this code while we're here.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
The reviewer questioned the functionality of follow_page_pte_commit(), noting that it performs additional actions beyond simply grabbing a folio, and requested further clarification on its purpose.

Reviewer David expressed concern about the inconsistent use of follow_page_pte_commit() and suggested it should be used in other places as well to maintain consistency.
reviews.raw_body:
It does more than grabbing, hm, let me think.

gup_grab_and_store_folio_pages()

not sure.

---

Yes, and my gut feeling is that the same helper should be also used in the other
places. Maybe there is no real bug there, but the inconsistency is concerning.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that moving gup_fill_pages() outside the lock is necessary for PUD path, but noted it's a noop on most architectures except s390.

Author acknowledged a potential issue with marking the folio dirty and losing data written to the page, but did not commit to addressing it.
sentiment_signals: did not commit to addressing it
reviews.raw_body:
It does more than grabbing, but if we want to
have the PUD path use this same function, we
will probably want to move the gup_fill_pages()
call to outside the lock.

At that point we'll be left with grabbing the
pages, and marking the folio dirty/accessed,
plus the arch_make_folio_accessible() call,
which seems to be a noop on anything but s390,
where it makes the page accessible to the
hypervisor (not sure when/why GUP needs this).

---

The page table dirty bits should ensure that we
don't lose any data written to the page, but not
marking the folio dirty might mess with dirty
balancing.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-08-12.patch_summary: This patch splits the function follow_page_pte() into two separate functions: follow_page_pte_commit() and follow_page_pte(). The new function, follow_page_pte_commit(), handles the per-folio work of grabbing a reference to the page, making it accessible if necessary, marking it dirty or accessed if required, and filling in the pages array. This change allows for more granular control over when the safety checks and commit operations are applied, without changing any functionality. The patch is part of an ongoing effort to improve the Linux kernel's memory management subsystem.
